verdict.rationale: Gemini documents a standing deprecations page that tracks announced earliest shutdown dates per model and marks already-shutdown models. A dated release-notes changelog records alias moves, and versioned model IDs stay pinnable while `-latest` aliases move on each release. This covers model-level versioning and deprecation tracking. However, the evidence does not document versioning of the API surface itself or a formal minimum-notice deprecation policy, so coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: documented API-surface versioning (e.g. stable vs beta endpoint versions), a formal deprecation policy with guaranteed minimum notice periods, independent/hands-on corroboration that pinned versions and shutdown dates are honored.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Deprecation announcements are made on the Release notes page, and the announced earliest shutdown dates are tracked on this page. Already-shutdown models are indicated
This is now the model behind `gemini-flash-latest`
Maintained "Release notes" changelog for the Gemini API — dated entries for model launches, alias moves, and feature releases
